1: The patient’s symptoms, radiographic findings, and the presence of a well-defined sclerotic margin in the submetaphyseal lytic lesion are consistent with Brodie’s abscess. The typical radiographic features of Brodie’s abscess include an oval-shaped area of decreased density, forming a lucent lesion, encased by a dense rim of reactive sclerosis, typically occurring at a metaphysis, most commonly that of the tibia.
